why: user 10-06 23:5x KST: cogito5170/Dev and cogito5170/Ops are where the Dev and Ops baselines are transplanted into the VM; the cloud keeps one external baseline (boundary). VM internals are encapsulated from the cloud but keep being updated by the automated pipeline. Cutover is a later, separate spec. Rev 2 (user 10-06 23:5x): message identifiers reuse our existing semantic forms instead of new header names.
constraints: never two primaries: until a later cutover spec the cloud Dev/Ops hubs stay the authority and the VM baselines take no externally visible action
cloud hubs are never deleted; after a later cutover they become a read-only archive (rollback reference)
no VM baseline runs a model continuously until the user sets a budget after ASK-VM-COST
LLM output inside the VM is a proposal/opinion only, never a decision
goal: Dev baseline and Ops baseline run inside the VM, each with its role, rules, notes and inbox held in its own repository (cogito5170/Dev, cogito5170/Ops), reachable from the cloud only through the protocol boundary.
acceptance: cogito5170/Dev and cogito5170/Ops each hold everything their baseline needs to run on the VM; neither depends on the baseline repo's ops/flow at runtime
the boundary admits only cloud->VM spec/1 and ask/1, and VM->cloud status/1, opinion/1, incident/1 and shadow/1; any other form or direction is rejected at the boundary and the rejection is recorded

boundary messages use only our existing semantic form fields, no new header names: the form name carries the version (spec/1 = version 1), id is the request identity, from / to / at are source, destination and time (flow.py), and a reply names the message it answers with ref (as in notify/1) = that message's id; a duplicate id is answered once
the cloud side operates without reading the Dev/Ops repositories, VM inbox, session state or internal logs; anything it needs arrives as a VM->cloud message
authority, routing, state transitions, admission/rejection and integration inside the VM are decided by deterministic rules; replaying the same input sequence gives the same decisions
VM internals can be updated by the automated pipeline (built release -> verified deploy) without changing the boundary; a boundary change is a new form version (/2), never a silent field change
after a VM restart the baselines resume from persisted state with no lost or duplicated message
